text:
Predicates:
SupervisedLearning(x) ::: x is a supervised learning algorithm.
UnsupervisedLearning(x) ::: x is an unsupervised learning algorithm.
ReinforcementLearning(x) ::: x is a reinforcement learning algorithm.
Uses(x, y) ::: x is used to train y.
Trains(x, y) ::: x trains y.
RequiresLabelledData(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
Model(y) ::: y is a model.
StateOfTheArt(y) ::: y is the state-of-the-art model.
Training(y, x) ::: y is trained with x.

Premises:
∀x (UnsupervisedLearning(x) → ¬Uses(x, y)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't use labelled data.
Model(y) ∧ StateOfTheArt(y) ::: The model is the state-of-the-art.
Training(y, x) ∧ Uses(x, y) ::: The state-of-the-art model is trained with certain algorithms.
¬Uses(x, y) for ReinforcementLearning(x) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the model.
RequiresLabelledData(x) ∧ Uses(x, y) ::: Machine learning algorithms for training the model require labelled data.

Conclusion:
∃x (SupervisedLearning(x) ∧ Uses(x, y)) ::: Supervised learning is used to train the model.
